turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung reassured O-lan, telling her that her words would guide their children and that she need not worry, for they would be well cared for.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan was anxious, she told Wang Lung, that her son should follow her words and not stray, for his future and that of his descendants depended on it.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son nodded, his voice soft and hesitant, as he told O-lan that he would follow her guidance and that her words would always be in his heart.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan nodded, her eyes welling with tears, and whispered to Wang Lung that she hoped her son would always remember her words and follow the path she had set for him.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung reassured O-lan, telling her that her son would always remember her words and that he, Wang Lung, would make sure that her last wishes were fulfilled.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan nodded, her voice trembling as she expressed her hope that Wang Lung would see to the marriage of her eldest son, to ensure a future for the family.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded, his eyes filled with determination, and promised O-lan that he would see to the marriage of their eldest son, come what may, to secure a future for their family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan squeezed Wang Lung's hand, her eyes fixed on the eldest son, and whispered that she hoped the marriage would bring him happiness and stability.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded, his voice steady as he assured O-lan that the marriage would indeed bring happiness and stability to their eldest son.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan's eyes softened, and she squeezed Wang Lung's hand tighter, whispering that she hoped the eldest son would find a good and kind wife, someone who would take care of him.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that he would find a good and kind wife for their eldest son, someone who would be a blessing to the family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan’s gaze softened further, her hand tightening around Wang Lung’s as she murmured, hoping the eldest son’s marriage would indeed bring peace to their troubled life.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded, his hand squeezing O-lan's in reassurance, telling her that the eldest son's marriage would indeed bring peace to their troubled life.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan’s grip on Wang Lung’s hand tightened, her voice barely above a whisper as she murmured about the need to prepare for the future, to ensure the family’s stability beyond her passing.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded, his hand squeezing O-lan's in reassurance, telling her that he would take care of everything, ensuring the family’s stability beyond her passing.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan’s eyes flickered between Wang Lung and their son, her voice trembling with the weight of her words as she urged Wang Lung to find a suitable match for the maid, ensuring her future alongside the eldest son’s.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid’s eyes flickered with concern as she whispered to O-lan, assuring her that she would do everything in her power to support the eldest son and ensure a stable future for all.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan’s gaze softened as she looked at the maid, her voice strained yet firm as she urged Wang Lung to find a match for the maid, ensuring her future stability and happiness.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded, squeezing O-lan's hand again, assuring her that he would find a suitable match for the maid, ensuring her future alongside the eldest son’s.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan’s voice wavered as she spoke again, urging Wang Lung to not forget the maid’s future and to ensure she finds happiness and stability in life.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
